_comment: Azure AI Search cost ceiling: SKU, replicas and partitions together.
WHY ALL THREE: AI Search is billed on search units, and
search units = replicas x partitions
so capping the SKU alone does not cap the cost. A 'standard' service at
12 replicas x 12 partitions is 144 search units.
WHY THIS EXISTS: no built-in allow-list policy for AI Search SKUs exists.
Verified 2026-09-25 - the only SKU-touching built-in is
a049bf77-880b-470f-ba6d-9f21c530cf83 ('Azure AI Search service should use
a SKU that supports private link'), whose rule is only
sku.name equals 'free'. It blocks the free tier; it cannot express an
allow-list and does nothing about the expensive end.
storage_optimized_l1 / storage_optimized_l2 and standard3 are deliberately
absent from the default allow-list.
ALIASES VERIFIED against the live provider:
Microsoft.Search/searchServices/sku.name
Microsoft.Search/searchServices/replicaCount
Microsoft.Search/searchServices/partitionCount
NOTE ON exists: replicaCount and partitionCount are optional on create and
default to 1. Each numeric test is guarded by an exists check so that an
omitted property is not treated as a violation.

properties.displayName: Azure AI Search services must stay within the approved SKU and scale ceiling
properties.description: Denies or audits Microsoft.Search services that use a SKU outside the approved list, or that exceed the approved replica or partition count. AI Search bills on search units (replicas x partitions), so all three are constrained together.

metadata.description: Audit reports without blocking. Deny blocks the deployment.
Permitted sku.name values. Lower-case, as emitted by the resource provider.
